column1: # Little Nightmares II: Tarsier Studios / Bandai Namco, Unreal Engine 4.25 (MallocBinned3, Wwise), SDK 10.4.1, NVN; update 1.4 (v262144). Two DLC NSPs are licences with no content.
# Started from the NSP script's provisional profile (dm/games/profile_guess.py) on Linux; the bring-up is done by reading the code and trying builds on an iPhone (no Mac at hand)

# Game name: only a label for profile listings and the Mac window title; the iOS app name is the game name in the base NSP, and the bundle ID comes from the base game title ID (build_ipa.sh / NSP script)
# load order as on Horizon: main, subsdk*, sdk (subsdk0 = NintendoSDK_movie)
# one version 8 pak (UE 4.22 to 4.25) holds everything: 4.9 GB, 43,523 files, none compressed, its index encrypted (uepak.py: the key is two 16-byte constants, split_keys)
# Unreal Engine 4.25: nninitStartup (main+0x1d0fe20, through the nninitStartup export) needs virtual address memory and reserves one address region for the engine, 62 GB unless
# -SwitchVirtualAddressSpaceSize= (MB) caps it (main+0x1d10138; the options come from nn::os::GetHostArgv, main+0x1d102b0); malloc gets a 3 MB block and the heap is 4 MB. Its allocator, an
# FMallocBinned3 made at run time by FPlatformMemory::BaseAllocator (main+0x1d10760), would reserve 37 pools of 1 GB of that region: the constructor call is cut and the host's allocator
# takes its place (patches.py, hle_uemalloc.c), as DRAGON QUEST VII Reimagined's. The SDK's node area is cut to 62 MB and large regions are 32 MB aligned (dm/tools/sdk_patches.py), so the
# 2 GB region starts 64 MB into the alias region. DRAGON QUEST VII Reimagined's layout: 3.125 GB alias region, 256 MB stacks, 384 MB heap region (the game sets 4 MB)
# the NPDM declares 80 MB of system resource
# The shaders are inline in the cooked packages and in Engine/GlobalShaderCache-GLSL_SWITCH.bin (shader_split.py ue_legacy_jobs): 20,170
